title: People Need a Route, Not a Shortcut to an Answer
description: I am giving people and agents a way through real material: a holdings hierarchy, a production ingestion path, project filtering, and tool wiring.
body:
A model that only a service can walk is still a private map. People need a route from a broad holding to a project, a record, and a passage. Agents need the same route, not an undocumented shortcut to a generated answer. If a record is missing, the question has to be traceable: not admitted, not classified, not indexed, filtered away, or simply unrelated.

I spent last night and this morning on an enterprise content hierarchy for ValeskaVision Holdings as an Alfresco site taxonomy, a StoryTeller ingestion path that can scan, classify, chunk, relate, and sync, a project filter, and MCP tools for episode-aware search. I started a search frontend the same night on a working branch. I am not treating that frontend as merged into the main line.

From a holding to a record

The hierarchy is a visible route through enterprise material, not a marketing sitemap. Ingestion supplies that route with records while keeping source context — for this drop, a defined production tree of text files, with a dry-run so the operation can be inspected. Project filtering narrows the field without asking a reader to remember every internal identifier. Episode and scene become types the model can name, which is a technical fact about this collection, not a claim that the professional site is now a story bible.

The MCP tools of this evening need a query and an episode number for the production search, and they can return episode context. That is a governed way for an assistant to walk the same route a person would, instead of inventing a second path. Capture-thought is fixed again so the memory service of March still answers. The search UI on the side branch — bar, cards, detail, chips for file, entity, and thought — is the shape of a human door. Until it sits on the main line, the human door is the hierarchy, the filter, and the records the read-only routes already expose.

Content model versions 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 are dated this same day in Alfresco. The last adds production metadata. That is taxonomy work. It is not a claim that the Innovators website now publishes story canon. Creative narrative remains where it belongs. I am recording the technical route here, not the stories.

Making the break visible

This is a different kind of progress from a more capable model. If a record is missing, the path can be examined in pieces: admission, classification, chunking, filter, query. That is operational. It does not say search is complete. It does not say the React frontend is the public site. It does not say VALESKA has become Alfresco, or that StoryTeller’s creative canon has moved onto this website. A holdings taxonomy and a production ingest script are how this organization files its own work. They are not a product announcement.

The next test

The next test is end-to-end on the main line: a question, a project filter, a record, and the underlying evidence, compared with what ingestion says should be there. The purpose is to learn where a reader’s path breaks before claiming that people can already find their way.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits 2b1f25e, a1be388, d03abd9, and c55d9f1. Author timestamps are 12 April 2026 local; UTC crosses 13 April, which is this article’s publication date. d03abd9 (search UI) landed on a working branch and is not treated as merged to main.

data.author: David Gargan
data.coverAlt: An observatory sending a stream of pictures, pages, and crystals across a night landscape: a route people can follow from a question toward a record, not a shortcut to an answer.
